page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, this server features 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU allocation is dedicated, and the processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the n4-standard-16 in the average performance tier across most workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1855.0 and a multi-core score of 11352.0. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 1107.55 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 117.6 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a large-block write speed of 67.32 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates strong performance in text generation using a small 135M LLM model, reaching 282.68 tokens/sec, while medium 7B model text generation operates at 12.18 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-16 offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it a standard choice for general-purpose workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, limiting its suitability for high-I/O databases or heavy deep learning training. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate database operations.

Lacking bundled local storage and GPUs, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Performance benchmarks place the server in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11352.0 and a static web serving throughput of 22.14 GB/sec. It demonstrates strong capabilities in small-model LLM text generation at 282.68 tokens/sec, alongside a Passmark database score of 7748.52. The n4-standard-16 is qualitatively cost-effective for standard workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe drives or hardware acceleration. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations.
